name: Streaming Do Smart Contracts Incur Higher Transaction Costs Than Traditional Contracts 4112Fa0866
text: Do Smart Contracts Incur Higher Transaction Costs than Traditional Contracts? argues that adapting institutional arrangements can cause smart contracts to incur higher transaction costs than traditional contracts. This directly challenges Kaal's proposition that smart contracting removes almost all transaction costs. The abstract frames the result as a possibility grounded in transaction-cost economics and does not provide an empirical cost estimate.
